label: late original-phase steps and <DEL> (t>=4), strongest when the sequence starts with d
explanation: Fires only at the end of the input: original-phase steps with t >= 4, plus the <DEL> step. Rate peaks at t = 5-6, and it is essentially silent at t <= 2 and through the copy phase (0.3% of mass, almost all at recall_idx 1). The predicate (phase<=1)&(t>=4) covers 99% of activation mass, but precision is only 0.18 because the feature is active on just about 17% of those steps. Which ones depends on the sequence content. First token d matters most for magnitude: restricting to orig(0)==d gives 0.97 precision and covers 59% of the top activation quartile, and first token i gives a weaker boost. Within a sequence it prefers first occurrences of a token (in_first) and inputs z or e. It does not fire on copy-phase outputs or on early original tokens. Without d at the start, activations are weak (about 0.1-0.3 of max) and sparse. No simple token rule recovers precision.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: d, i, m, a, 0, c; least: j, e, n, g) and the current input token, by phase (input phase: z, e, t, x; copy phase: d, f, i, m; delimiter step: <DEL>); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
